newsitem.title: UK: British fantasy has McCartney, Diana in cabinet.
newsitem.headline: British fantasy has McCartney, Diana in cabinet.

text.p: Paul McCartney is in the running for Prime Minister along with Princess Diana and entrepreneur Richard Branson.
Britons can now indulge their political fantasies in the run-up to a general election, thanks to the New Statesman magazine.
Trying to inject a note of fun into the pre-election fever now sweeping Britain's media, the magazine on Friday adapted a game already played by sports fans across the country.
Instead of picking your dream soccer or cricket team, and scoring points based on their prowess from game to game, readers were asked to select their ideal cabinet in "Fantasy Politics".

The cabinet members, who range from politicians and sportsmen to pop stars and scientists, will be rated on a highly subjective view of their performance in the media week by week in the run-up to the election Prime Minister John Major must call by May.
So Diana, following her successful trip to Angola to highlight the dangers of landmines, could this week make a far better foreign minister than Malcolm Rifkind, the incumbent.
"The panel will of course award negative points for stupid remarks, bad hair-days (disastrous performances), punch-ups in TV studios etc," the New Statesman said.
The winners of each weekly round will get two bottles of whisky. The final round will coincide with the election.
But the political magazine, closely aligned with Labour leader Tony Blair, issued a warning to the real politicians.
"Being deliberately boring is tantamount to a professional foul in Fantasy Politics and attracts a yellow card. If it continues the player will be red-carded and suspended," it said.
